text:
From highest to lowest, U.S. law runs: the U.S. Constitution, then treaties and federal statutes (roughly coequal, with the later-in-time one controlling), then executive agreements, then state law. Under the Supremacy Clause, valid federal law overrides conflicting state law. This replaces my earlier answer, which omitted executive agreements and added federal regulations and local ordinances as separate tiers.

CONFIDENCE: 80
